focused_rust_libraries.command: cargo test --offline -p phone-host -p phone-runtime -p phone-app-device -p phone-native -p phone-android -p phone-ios -p phone-platform-desktop -p phone-alarm-service -p phone-system -p phone-state --lib
focused_rust_libraries.scope: Focused Linux-host library tests, including runtime cancellation and reentrant completion, host/document leases, closed media ownership, catalog revision/pin identity and foreground alarm lifecycle. The isolated GIO test is invoked by its parent test; the opt-in MPRIS test belongs to a separate protocol gate. Mobile tests here exercise portable contracts, not target compilation.

javascript.scope: Controlled host/browser and service-worker boundaries, including activation encoding, bounded platform tasks, suspension, cancellation and closure. These are not rendered browser or OS permission tests.

packaging.scope: Linux session staging and Windows per-account shell configuration generation, including the Python 3.15 reserved-path API compatibility regression. No machine session or policy was changed.

compile.scope: Shared composition and native Wayland/X11 entry points type-checked locally. Local Linux media/camera development libraries were absent, so unavailable-provider bridges were used. The browser host type-check is not a WebAssembly build. Full desktop links, browser WebAssembly, APKs and UIKit Simulator execution are recorded separately from GitHub Actions.

limits: Local checks do not establish physical camera/audio playback, permission dialogs, notification delivery, location accuracy or installed-launcher behavior.
Linux compositor login and Windows Shell Launcher configuration were generated and validated but not installed into a running session.
Background alarm wake-up, carrier services, original cloud accounts and XAP/APPX execution are outside this implementation.
These checks do not establish original-device pixel or motion parity.
